structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: This letter from Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) to stock exchanges (NSE and BSE) serves as a notice for the 30th Annual General Meeting (AGM) and submission of the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25. It states the AGM will be held on June 19, 2025, at 3:00 p.m. IST via video conferencing/other audio-visual means. The Integrated Annual Report containing the AGM notice is submitted under SEBI Listing Regulations, sent electronically to members, and uploaded on TCS's website. The letter includes contact and registration details, is signed by the Company Secretary, and is copied to depositories (NSDL, CDSL, MUFG Intime).

structure.title: Our Founder
structure.summary: The text honors two Tata leaders. It introduces founder Jamsetji Nusserwanji Tata (1839–1904) with his quote on community as business's purpose. It then memorializes Padma Vibhushan Ratan N. Tata (1937–2024), expressing loss and praising his uncommon leadership that shaped the Tata Group and India. It highlights his commitment to excellence, integrity, and innovation, which expanded the group globally while maintaining moral direction. It notes his philanthropy in education and healthcare benefiting millions, his humility, and his enduring legacy as an inspiration.

structure.title: Annual Report_V1_2025
structure.summary: This annual report section covers TCS's FY2025 performance and strategy. It begins with a tribute to Ratan Tata, then provides a table of contents and details the 'Perpetually Adaptive Enterprise' theme. It includes board and management information, Chairman and CEO letters highlighting AI integration and financial results (US$30 billion revenue), and a year-in-review of partnerships, awards, and the London Marathon. It outlines the integrated business model and value creation through five capitals: financial (revenue growth, margins), human (talent acquisition, development), intellectual (research, patents), social (CSR, customer trust), and natural (emissions reduction, water conservation). Customer stories showcase AI applications in drug design, employee experience, telecommunications, electoral roll management, logistics, airline operations, net-zero grids, media analysis, banking, education, and custodial operations.

nodes.title: Remembering Mr. Tata
nodes.summary: The text is a tribute to Mr. Ratan N. Tata, noting his dates and titles, and expressing loss at his passing. It highlights his role as an uncommon leader who shaped the Tata Group and the nation, describing him as more than a chairperson who inspired by example. It mentions his commitment to excellence, integrity, and innovation, and how the Tata Group expanded globally under his stewardship while maintaining its moral compass. It also covers his philanthropy and societal development efforts in education and healthcare, which have impacted millions, and notes his genuine humility. The text concludes that his legacy will inspire continued adherence to his principles. Additionally, it includes a table of contents for an Integrated Annual Report 2024-25, listing sections such as Introduction, Performance Review, and Integrated Reporting Framework with specific page numbers and topics like About TCS, Board of Directors, letters from the Chairman and CEO, awards, and integrated business model components.

nodes.title: Letter from the CEO 1
nodes.summary: A CEO letter to shareholders reporting FY2025 milestones: revenues over US$30 billion and brand value over US$20 billion. nodes.title: Customer Stories
nodes.summary: This text highlights a pharmaceutical company's partnership with TCS to leverage AI for novel drug design against pancreatic cancer. It details the challenge of limited target-specific ligand datasets and TCS's solution: a de novo drug design pipeline using proprietary GenAI models (ligand-based, structure-based, gene expression-based) and predictive AI models for ADMET, binding affinity, and toxicity. The technology, deployed on AWS with NVIDIA T100, enabled the design of over 1,300 novel molecules, with 290 shortlisted and 12 selected for in-vitro assessment. The solution accelerated drug design, reducing the usual 12-month cycle by over 80% to eight weeks, cutting costs and saving expert resources. A second customer story briefly mentions an AI-driven employee experience transformation.

Revolutionizing Employee Experience with GenAl
TCS engineered a transformative platform, GenAI-powered digital concierge, that delivers personalized self-service while functioning as a technology-enabled talent marketplace. This platform, serving over 100,000 global users, seamlessly integrates essential business functions across more than 35 applications, enabling efficient workflows for over 850 scenarios in diverse domains including learning & development, human capital management, finance, procurement, partner affairs, marketing & sales, hoteling, risk management, legal, and IT services. Leveraging data-driven insights, the platform has significantly improved employee engagement, resulting in a 2% increase in employee productivity and generating substantial savings for the organization.

nodes.title: Transforming Telecommunications with GenAI
nodes.summary: Proximus, a connectivity and digital services provider, partnered with TCS on AI and GenAI interventions across business and IT functions. Business initiatives include streamlining sales processes from chaotic to self-healing by identifying customer journey friction points via behavioral analysis, optimizing sales order processes, and driving insights through proactive monitoring. IT transformation focuses on efficiency in software development and operations, using GenAI-powered development for productivity, and predictive maintenance through proactive IT operations monitoring for cost savings. Outcomes include real-time personalized promotions, improved customer experience, accelerated product launches, and enhanced developer productivity.

nodes.title: Customer Stories Digital Transformation of Electoral Roll Management in India
nodes.summary: The Election Commission of India partnered with TCS to develop ERO Net 2.0, a web-based application that digitalized electoral roll management nationwide. The app manages the end-to-end elector lifecycle with a centralized database and a daily-updated executive dashboard providing a 360-degree view. It enables citizens to update and search their details via EPIC or personal information, and generates voter information slips. TCS also created a printing tool that reduced distribution time and enhanced data security. The suite includes a BLO mobile app used to print over 25 crore EPICs and nearly 125 crore voter slips, with over 78 crore electors verified through house-to-house surveys. Rolled out nationwide in 7 months, it supports over 1.05 million officials in registrations, updates, and deletions, making voting more accessible, secure, and inclusive.

nodes.title: Customer Stories A journey towards becoming the most trusted advisor
nodes.summary: The text presents two customer stories. First, Commonwealth Bank of Australia sold its wealth business to KKR, creating independent Colonial First State (CFS), which needed to transition its IT estate, build systems, manage 30+ vendors, and serve 1 million customers. TCS, a decade-long partner, provided a transition roadmap, built an AWS cloud foundation, reimagined document management with IP solutions, used its Co-Innovation Network for rapid prototyping, and supported rebranding. The result is a scalable cloud-first platform positioning CFS as an industry leader. Second, a global logistics provider facing porch piracy and fraud (44 million packages lost/stolen in 2023, US$5 billion) partnered with TCS to implement an AI-powered solution using advanced analytics and petabytes of data to generate a 'Confidence score' predicting address-level shipping risks, enabling rerouting of high-risk packages, smarter shipping decisions, a new revenue stream, and potential annual savings of US$500 million.

nodes.title: AI: The Game Changer for Logistics and Supply Chain
nodes.summary: A leading global airline sought AI to enable self-service data decisions but faced multiple data platforms hindering speed, time-to-market, and increasing costs. Partnering with TCS, it unified functions under a manageable architecture for self-service analytics. Modernization included a business glossary for AI to interpret data, enabling natural language 'talk-to-data' for faster insights and decisions. TCS delivered a customized no-code data platform replacing proprietary tools while retaining features, making information accessible to non-technical users across Marketing, Customer Loyalty, Operations, Engineering, Revenue Management, and other divisions.

TCS was selected to lead back-office transformation across Finance, Procurement, HR, Service Desk, and Digital & Technology in over 100 countries. TCS delivered a balanced solution that standardized processes, enhanced customer experience, reduced onboarding time and aging debts, improved security, and optimized costs. It also helps the British Council adapt to global regulatory changes. A quote from Eleanor Hampson highlights accelerated transformation, efficiency, cost savings, and strengthened global operations.

Derivative financial instruments and hedging activity
The Group’s revenue is denominated in various foreign currencies. Given the nature of the business, a large portion of the costs are denominated in Indian Rupee. This exposes the Group to currency fluctuations.
The Board of Directors has constituted a Risk Management Committee (RMC) to frame, implement and monitor the risk management plan of the Group which inter-alia covers risks arising out of exposure to foreign currency fluctuations. Under the guidance and framework provided by the RMC, the Group uses various derivative instruments such as foreign exchange forward, currency options and futures contracts in which the counter party is generally a bank.
The following are outstanding currency options contracts, which have been designated as cash flow hedges:

It also covers derivative instruments not in hedging relationships, such as foreign exchange forwards, currency options, and futures, with aggregate notional amounts, fair values, and exchange gains/losses recognized. Additionally, it discloses expected transfer of losses from hedging reserve, maximum hedge period, and sensitivity analysis showing the impact of 10% appreciation or depreciation of underlying foreign currencies on other comprehensive income.

nodes.title: Financial risk management
nodes.summary:
Financial risk management
The Group is exposed primarily to fluctuations in foreign currency exchange rates, credit, liquidity and interest rate risks, which may adversely impact the fair value of its financial instruments. The Group has a risk management policy which covers risks associated with the financial assets and liabilities. The risk management policy is approved by the Board of Directors. The focus of the risk management committee is to assess the unpredictability of the financial environment and to mitigate potential adverse effects on the financial performance of the Group.
Market risk
Market risk is the risk that the fair value or future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate because of changes in market prices. Such changes in the values of financial instruments may result from changes in the foreign currency exchange rates, interest rates, credit, liquidity and other market changes. The Group’s exposure to market risk is primarily on account of foreign currency exchange rate risk.

nodes.title: • Foreign currency exchange rate risk

It also covers interest rate risk, noting limited exposure due to fixed-rate investments, and credit risk, including definitions, control measures, and expected credit loss references.
